chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The owner of the deposit and the owner of the merchandise are both entrusted (liable only for negligence).
And he (peace be upon him) said: When the borrowed item perishes with the borrower, he is not liable (for compensation) unless a condition was stipulated upon him.
And he (peace be upon him) said in another Hadith: When he is a just Muslim, there is no liability upon him.

key_terms.مُؤْتَمَنَانِ: Two entrusted ones (liable only for negligence)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions under which a borrower is liable for the loss of a borrowed item in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between 'daman' (strict liability) and 'amanah' (trusteeship), establishing that depositors and borrowers are generally liable only for negligence unless a specific condition is stipulated. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that a just Muslim ('adl) borrower is exempt from guaranteeing the loss of a borrowed item, reflecting the broader legal maxim of 'al-amanah la daman fiha' (trusteeship entails no guarantee).

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The owner of the entrustment and the merchandise are both entrusted’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the borrowed item perishes with the borrower, he would not be responsible except if there happened to be a stipulation upon him’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said in another Hadeeth: ‘When he was a just Muslim, so there is no liability upon him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “About the case of a man who claims that Wadi‘ah (safe deposit) were entrusted assets, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If a borrowed item is destroyed with the borrower he is not held liable
In another Hadith it is said that if the borrower is a just Muslim he is not held liable.
